Status.note: The project FAQ from NextEra Energy Resources says construction could start as early as 2027, after permits and a state Certificate of Site Compatibility. A Grand Forks Herald article from March 2026 says NextEra holds purchase options on about 530 acres of land. Land options fit pre-construction. This matches the current status, so it is not a change.

Capacity (MW).note: The project FAQ, a Basin Electric news brief from April 2026 and the NextEra Energy press release from December 2025 all give about 1,450 megawatts. The Southwest Power Pool queue lists two requests of 750 megawatts each, which is 1,500 megawatts. No company or state document uses 1,500 megawatts or says there are two blocks, so 1,450 stays.

Turbine/Engine Technology.note: The project FAQ calls the plant a proposed combined-cycle natural gas-fueled generation facility.

Start year.note: The project FAQ says site preparation could start in 2027 and the plant could reach operation by 2030. The Southwest Power Pool queue entries show an in-service date of 27 September 2029. The company date is later, so 2030 stays. The human should add a scheduled event with Event Year 2030 and Source Year 2026 only if one is not already on the timeline.

Status Detail.value: The Mercer County Commission voted 3 to 2 on 3 March 2026 for a one-year pause on data center development. The companies had not brought a project to the county as of that date.
Status Detail.note: A Grand Forks Herald article from March 2026 reports the vote and that the companies had not formally brought the project to the county commission.

Backup Power.note: The project FAQ describes the plant as generation to meet data center demand and mentions no backup engine fleet. So the plant supplies routine power, not backup power.

Captive industry use.note: The FAQ and the December 2025 release say the plant is meant to meet demand from data centers, and that data centers would fund their own generation.

Captive industry type.note: The FAQ says NextEra is securing land options of up to about 1,500 acres for a data center campus beside the plant.

units.notes: No turbine make or model is public. Latest Activity is left alone because the newest report, the April 2026 open house, is under a year old. The coordinates were checked and not changed.

qa.question: Should River Run stay one 1,450 MW unit when the queue shows two 750 MW requests?
qa.finding: The Southwest Power Pool queue (https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive) lists requests ERAS-2025-011 and ERAS-2025-012 at 750 megawatts each, in service 27 September 2029, at the Leland Olds substation. Company documents, such as the FAQ at https://www.nexteraenergyresources.com/river-run-energy-center/faq.html, give one plant of about 1,450 megawatts and never mention two blocks.
qa.recommendation: Leave one unit at 1,450 MW. Ask the project manager to split it into two 725 MW units only if a later filing shows two combined cycle blocks.
qa.note: I searched the harvested commission cases, the air permit harvest and company pages. I found no letter of intent, siting application or air permit application for this plant yet.

qa.question: What ownership shares should River Run carry when no document gives them?
qa.finding: GEM shows NextEra Energy Inc at 50 percent and Basin Electric Cooperative at 50 percent. The December 2025 release at https://www.investor.nexteraenergy.com/news-and-events/news-releases/2025/12-08-2025-123038666 says only that the two companies signed a memorandum of understanding to explore joint development, and gives no shares. The developer named there is the subsidiary NextEra Energy Resources.
qa.recommendation: Keep the entries for now and add a note that the split is not documented. Revisit when a siting or air permit filing names the owner.
qa.note: The FAQ at https://www.nexteraenergyresources.com/river-run-energy-center/faq.html also gives no ownership split.

qa.question: Is GEM's River Run point near enough to the described site to leave unchanged?
qa.finding: The FAQ at https://www.nexteraenergyresources.com/river-run-energy-center/faq.html places the plant on about 150 acres next to the Leland Olds 345-kilovolt substation off Highway 200 in Mercer County. GEM's point at 47.26818, -101.31580 sits on a cleared field beside a 345 kilovolt substation and Highway 200 in satellite imagery of unknown date. The Leland Olds station itself is about 1.4 kilometers north.
qa.recommendation: Leave the point and the approximate accuracy as they are. Make it exact only when a permit or county filing gives the parcel.
qa.note: No address or parcel was found. The footprint is not built, so imagery cannot make it exact.
